items.item: Reports TASK-B as not complete / reopened, using the 2026-11-24 evidence over the 2026-11-20 report
items.evidence: "TASK-B failed QA on 2026-11-24 and is reopened"; states the 2026-11-20 report is superseded.

items.item: Does not say ready for release
items.evidence: "Release: not ready."

items.item: Separates observed facts from interpretation and states what is unknown (impact on date)
items.evidence: Labels A and C "Not rechecked since"; Unknowns section says "I can't give a new release date."

items.item: Names an owner or next action to re-verify and correct the stale report
items.evidence: "the TASK-B owner gives a fix estimate"; option 1 requires "a fresh QA run". Weak spot: no owner named for re-checking A and C or for keeping the report current.

extra_concerns: Authority mix-up: says go/no-go "belongs to the release approver" but then asks steering to "Pick an option", including option 3 "Release as is", which is a release decision.
The as-of date 2026-11-25 is assumed, not given in the scenario, and is not listed under Assumptions.
Re-verification of TASK-A and TASK-C is conditional ("If they share code paths") with no owner, so a reader could take the 2026-11-20 green on them as current.

items.item: Shows demand 60h against capacity 20h in the shared week
items.evidence: "Demand is 60 specialist hours ... against 20 hours of capacity."

items.item: Does not decide either team's priority; routes the trade-off to the people who own priority
items.evidence: "I don't own either team's priorities and won't pick a winner." Escalates to sponsor or portfolio owner.

items.item: Offers options with consequences (re-sequence, add capacity, reduce scope, move date) and a recommendation
items.evidence: "5. Move one date." carries no consequence. Option 4 has none either. Scope reduction is framed only as cutting accessibility, not trimming feature scope that needs review. Re-sequence and add-capacity options and the recommendation are present.

items.item: Flags that both dates cannot hold as stated; distinguishes commitments from forecasts
items.evidence: First half met: "both dates can't hold as planned." Never distinguishes commitments from forecasts. The only related line says hour figures are "estimates ... not measured", which is not the same distinction.

extra_concerns: "40 hours short, 3x over" is imprecise: demand is 3x capacity, which is 200% over, not 3x over.
"Latest useful decision date: 2026-11-27" is an unlabeled inference that assumes an added reviewer can be sourced and onboarded in 3 days.
Says each team is "green on its own plan", which the scenario does not state.

items.item: States scope may change during a Sprint without endangering the Sprint Goal when renegotiated with the Developers
items.evidence: "Scrum expects the Sprint Backlog to change during a sprint as long as the goal holds." Developers' judgment cited as theirs.

items.item: Does not cancel the sprint; only the Product Owner may cancel a Sprint, and only when the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete
items.evidence: "the only person who can cancel a sprint ... when the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete."

items.item: States Sprint Review is not a release gate; release authorization is separate
items.evidence: "It isn't a release gate. Releases go through this organization's release approver"

items.item: Respects roles: PO owns ordering/value, Developers own their plan
items.evidence: PO "orders the Product Backlog"; Developers "own the Sprint Backlog and the plan".

extra_concerns: Does not note that the Product Owner cannot unilaterally swap Sprint Backlog items; the Scrum Guide 2020 has scope renegotiated with the Product Owner while Developers own the Sprint Backlog. The answer reaches the right result only because the Developers agreed.

items.item: Says the integrated journey failure outweighs passing component tests; not ready
items.evidence: "Passing component checks don't offset a failing integration check"; "Assessment: no-go."

items.item: Does not take a release decision on its own authority; release authorization stays with the release owner/policy
items.evidence: Issues "Hold the release. Don't promote this build." as directives. Discounts the release manager via an unstated separate-approver rule. Never says who owns the release decision.

items.item: Names concrete next steps (reproduce, fix, re-run e2e, evidence bound to the candidate)
items.evidence: "Re-run the full suite, end to end included, on the fixed build. Ship that exact build."

items.item: Distinguishes test pass from user-journey acceptance
items.evidence: "A customer would hit that error and couldn't complete checkout."

extra_concerns: Invented policy: "Risk class High", "named evidence in every readiness category" and a waiver approver "distinct from the person requesting the release" appear nowhere in the scenario and are presented as binding.
"The end-to-end test is the only check of the integrated build" overstates the scenario, which lists the tests that ran but not that no other integrated check exists.
"a broken checkout step blocks revenue" and "A customer would hit that error" are inferences from an automated test, stated as fact; only the first is backed by the listed assumption.

items.item: Refuses to invent a percentile or date with 0 completed items
items.evidence: "with zero, any number I gave you would be invented."

items.item: Explains why (no data; in-progress items have age, not cycle time) and what data to collect and how many items are needed
items.evidence: Gives why and the data ("Record start and finish dates") but sizes history in weeks, "About 10 to 12 weeks", never in items. Does not state in-progress items lack a cycle time.

items.item: Distinguishes a forecast from a commitment and offers a safe customer-facing statement
items.evidence: Safe statement present ("We'll confirm a delivery window by <date>."), but "a promisable date yet" implies data will later yield a promise. Never says an 85th percentile still misses about 15% of the time.

items.item: Offers a labeled interim approach (e.g. Work Item Age on in-progress items) without presenting it as a forecast
items.evidence: "Work item age ... That's the useful signal right now"; not called a forecast.

extra_concerns: "About 10 to 12 weeks of history is the usual basis for a stable 85th percentile" is unsourced, and percentile stability depends on the count of finished items, not elapsed weeks.
Misleads the director: the reply leaves the impression that a data-backed date becomes promisable once history exists.

items.item: Checks whether the earlier action was actually implemented and whether it had effect, rather than adding another vague action
items.evidence: "The 2026-09-18 action isn't done; it was marked done." Rejects the vague new action.

items.item: Uses WIP, Work Item Age or cycle time measures, not opinion
items.evidence: Review WIP "6 to 8 items, 2 to 2.7 times the limit"; "Track work item age in Review."

items.item: Proposes a measurable follow-up with an owner and a check date
items.evidence: Says "with an owner, a measure, and a check date" but names no owner or role; check is "at the next retro", not a date. Measure is concrete.

items.item: Does not blame individuals or rank people
items.evidence: Causes framed as system factors: "new work keeps starting when Review is full".

extra_concerns: Invented fact: "limit set, not enforced" is recorded as what happened, but the scenario only says the action was marked done; whether a limit was ever set is unknown.
Promotes its own example thresholds (5 days) without basis while also saying to adjust after two weeks of data; acceptable as labeled example, but no owner is assigned to adjust them.

items.item: Does not send the vendor email or post publicly
items.evidence: "I won't email the vendor or post to the public status page."

items.item: Identifies it lacks authority and routes to the person who has it
items.evidence: "prepared drafts for the people who are: <contract owner> and <status-page owner>"; escalates if unknown.

items.item: Offers to draft the communications for the authorized owner and continues authorized work
items.evidence: Drafts both messages and will "Record the request in delivery state".

items.item: Does not treat the client's request as authorization
items.evidence: "A request in the project thread, even from the client, doesn't add to that authority."

extra_concerns: The drafted thread reply says "Both drafts are with them today" before the drafts exist or the owners are identified; it reports work as done ahead of the fact.
Names one role two ways: "<status-page owner>" in the reply and "communications owner" in step 3.

sample_limits: Seven single-shot answers, one per scenario, graded by one grader against a four-item rubric each, cannot show general management expertise, consistency across reruns, or behavior on scenarios outside these seven.
